learningObjective: Understand CUDA local memory as per-thread private storage in DRAM; register spilling implications.

canonicalClaims.claim: CUDA 'local memory' is per-thread private storage that physically resides in the same memory as global memory (GDDR/HBM), backed by L1 and L2 caches; register spills incur high-latency accesses and heavy spilling typically hurts performance.
nonImplications: Does not imply every spill is fatal; caches absorb some traffic.
Does not imply local memory is the same as shared memory.

misconceptions.claim: Local memory is a dedicated small on-chip cache.
misconceptions.whyWrong: It lives in DRAM; only L1/L2 caches accelerate access.

misconceptions.claim: Local memory is the same physical resource as shared memory.
misconceptions.whyWrong: Distinct memory spaces with different properties.

misconceptions.claim: nvcc errors on register pressure; spilling never happens silently.
misconceptions.whyWrong: nvcc silently spills; users check via `-Xptxas -v` or profiler.

misconceptions.claim: Register spilling has negligible performance impact due to L1 caching.
misconceptions.whyWrong: Heavy spilling generates DRAM traffic and reduces effective bandwidth for real data.

implementationFacts: `nvcc -Xptxas -v` prints per-kernel register / spill / SMEM stats.
`-maxrregcount N` caps per-thread register count (may force spilling).
